**Tier:** T3 (native configuration: adds a native module and changes the binary's update behaviour)
**Why:** Owner 10-01 10:44 approved over-the-air updates for the clinic binary. With `expo-updates` in the binary, JavaScript-only fixes after approval ship the same day without a new store review. Expo Free plan only (EAS Update free tier, no paid EAS features, no custom EAS environments).
**T4 trigger scan:** none. No auth, entitlement, payments, PII or migration; no CI gate file (`.github/workflows/*`, `scripts/ci/*`) is touched. No secret added: the updates URL is public, update signing is not enabled.
**T3 trigger scan:** yes. New native dependency (`expo-updates ~56.0.28`); `runtimeVersion {policy: fingerprint}` and `updates` config in app.json; a `channel` per eas.json build profile, including a new `clinic` channel; Android `versionCode` 4→5.
**Bounded T1:** `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md`; validator/guard scripts and their tests.
**Builder/owner:** Claude Opus 5.5 (S-RELEASE-MOB, agent 112; earlier rounds by the clinic wave-1 builder). Owner: operator. Needs an independent audit at the exact head plus green CI.
**Acceptance evidence:** see "Round 3" below (targeted jest 139/139 + fingerprint 2/2 locally; CI runs tsc + full suites).
**Promotion triggers:** enabling update code signing; changing the runtime policy after a store build has shipped; any `checkAutomatically` / `fallbackToCacheTimeout` change; any change to the purchase gate file or its lock.

---

## Round 3 (S-RELEASE-MOB, agent 112): brought to main + clinic channel → head `17b5a70`, CI fix → `92c25ec`

### How this branch was brought to main
#304 (this PR's old base, `clinic/m2-core-polish`) was **squash-merged** into main (9c6d8bf), so the m2 commits this branch carried are not ancestors of main and a plain merge conflicted in 18 #304 files. Resolution, as one merge commit (`147614f`, parents 4578715 + main 2c17c241, no history rewrite, no force push): **every file takes main's version**, then this PR's own delta (`3d9ab11..4578715`: expo-updates, runtime policy, channels, guard, validator, docs, tests) is re-applied on top. Net diff vs main is only this PR's files. Base retargeted to `main`.
- iOS `buildNumber` stays at main's `"6"`; Android `versionCode` 4 → 5 (unchanged intent).
- `scripts/purchase-policy.sha256` re-pinned to main's reviewed gate file (`493550ba…`; the file changed only through the #304 merge). The fingerprint mutations (threshold 6→600, always-show) still apply to main's file.
- Lockfile: the 7 new entries applied cleanly to main's lock; every dependency range was checked with semver against main's resolved versions.

### New: the clinic binary has its own update channel
Main gained a `clinic` build profile (`extends: production`) with clinic-only flags in `eas.json` env (`EXPO_PUBLIC_FF_CLIENT_TUTORIAL`, `_COMMUNITY_TAB/HALL/COHORTS`, `_COACH_BRIEF`, `_CONSULTATION_ONBOARDING`, `_COMMUNITY_DM=false`). Through `extends` it would have inherited channel `production`, and `eas update` **does not apply eas.json build env** (Expo docs), so any production update would have reached clinic devices with every clinic feature off.
| Change | Where | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `clinic.channel = "clinic"`, `clinic.environment = "production"` (explicit) | `eas.json` | `validateAppConfigUpdates.test.js` repo-config case |
| `scripts/eas-profile.js` resolves `extends` like EAS (child wins, `env` merged) | new | guard `loadChannels` case |
| Guard: channels come from eas.json; `--environment` must equal the profile's environment (`clinic` → `production`); a channel shared by two profiles refuses | `scripts/eas-update-guard.js` | `checkArgs` cases |
| Guard build parity: the publish child gets the resolved profile env (clinic flags, `TGP_ANDROID_HEALTH_CONNECT=0`, which also keeps the config fingerprint equal to the build's); every other local `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` is dropped; the hide flag still comes only from EAS. eas-cli exports with `{...process.env, ...EAS env}` (EAS wins), so the guard reads `eas env:list <env> --format short` for project and account scope and refuses when a same-name variable differs, is masked or duplicated, or when a list fails | same | 7 refusal cases + clinic publish + identical-copy accepted |
| Guard: every `kind: "required"` name in `config/expected-env.json` must be present in EAS or the profile env | same | "required name missing" case |
| Validator: clinic profile/channel/environment required; hide flag checked after `extends`; one profile per channel | `scripts/validate-app-config.js` | 7 new mutation cases |

### Prior finding C4 (GPT 6.1 Sol @ 45787152) — closed
`updates.enabled` must be `true` (was a warning) and `checkAutomatically` must be exactly `ON_LOAD` (was any valid mode). 4 new mutation cases.

### Launch and offline behaviour
`fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0` (launch never waits on the network; the update check runs natively in the background) and `checkAutomatically: ON_LOAD`. No JS code calls `expo-updates`, so a failed/offline check has no JS path that can throw. Anti-bricking and the embedded update cannot be disabled (validator). Device proof is still required (below).

### OTA release procedure (operator-run; also in `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md`)
1. One-time: the Expo project owner enables EAS Update for project `a12c3345-…` (expo.dev → Updates). Provision `EXPO_PUBLIC_FF_IOS_HIDE_NON_P2P_PURCHASES=true` (plaintext) and the release `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values in EAS `production` and `preview`. Restrict publish rights to the owner.
2. The first binary built from main after this merges is the first OTA-capable one; older binaries never receive updates.
3. For each JS fix: merge to main; check out that commit; `npx expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve --platform ios|android` must equal the target build's runtime on expo.dev (otherwise ship a binary).
4. `npm run update:publish -- --channel clinic --environment production --message "<what changed>" --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run` (production: `--channel production --environment production`; internal: `--channel preview --environment preview`). Publish to `preview` first and check on a preview build.
5. Roll back with `eas update:rollback` or republish the previous commit through the guard.
Hard gate before the first production/clinic publish (not performed, not provable in Jest): offline cold start twice, preview update received, a clinic update reaches only the clinic binary, early-crash recovery to the embedded bundle, rollback received.

### Prior findings (Sol @ 45787152) disposition
- **B1** inherited #304 blockers: #304 was fixed, audited and merged; this tree now carries main's #304 code verbatim (no m2 files differ from main).
- **C1** Supabase Hermes pin: #307 is on main; this tree has main's lock plus 7 expo-updates entries only.
- **C2** device checks: still a hard pre-publish gate (unchanged, listed above).
- **C3** unsigned updates / governance: unchanged posture, documented; the guard is governance, not an authorization boundary.
- **C4**: closed (above).

### Tests (Round 3)
```
heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand scripts/__tests__/expectedEnv.test.js scripts/__tests__/expoModuleGradleGuard.test.js \
  scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfig.test.js scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfigUpdates.test.js scripts/__tests__/easUpdateGuard.test.js
  -> 5 suites, 139 passed
heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand scripts/__tests__/purchaseGateFingerprint.test.js   -> 2 passed (ios, android)
node scripts/validate-app-config.js                                               -> OK (2 pre-existing warnings)
```
Local deps lack `expo-updates` (shared install from main); CI's clean `npm ci` + tsc + full suites are the evidence at the head.

## Fix rounds
| Round | Head | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1b88f42 | AUDIT_mobile_305_e186e06e | Fixed (history below) |
| 2 | 0897487 | AUDIT_mobile_305_1b88f424 | Fixed (history below) |
| 2b | 4578715 | Sol @45787152 B1 / C1 / C2 / C3 / C4 | B1 closed by main's #304; C1 #307 on main; C2 device checks stay a hard gate; C3 governance documented; C4 fixed in 17b5a70 (`updates.enabled` true + `checkAutomatically: ON_LOAD` enforced) |
| 3 | 17b5a70 | Base #304 squash-merged; clinic channel missing | Merged main 2c17c24 (147614f); clinic channel + `environment` + guard parity |
| 3b | 92c25ec | CI: `androidHealthConnectConfig.test.js` (from main) pinned versionCode 4; this PR bumps to 5 (6 failures) | Test asserts app.json's value is unchanged and pins 5; `src/config/__tests__` 104/104 locally |

# Earlier rounds (history)

**Tier:** T3 (native configuration: adds a native module and changes the binary's update behaviour)
**Why:** PLAN §4 default 4. With `expo-updates` in build 6, JavaScript-only fixes after approval can ship the same day without a new App Review. It also bumps build numbers for the next TestFlight/Play upload.
**T4 trigger scan:** none. No auth, entitlement, payments, PII or migration. No secret added: the updates URL is public, and code signing is not enabled.
**T3 trigger scan:** yes. New native dependency (`expo-updates ~56.0.28`, pinned by `npx expo install` for SDK 56). New `runtimeVersion` and `updates` config in app.json. `channel` added per eas.json build profile. `ios.buildNumber` 5→6, `android.versionCode` 4→5.
**Bounded T1:** `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md`; validator guard plus its tests.
**Builder/owner:** Claude Opus 5.5 (builder, clinic wave 1 mobile). Owner: operator; the Expo project owner does a one-time EAS Update enablement. Needs 1 independent audit plus green CI.
**Acceptance evidence:**
- `npm run validate:config` is OK and now enforces the updates config.
- 32/32 validator tests pass (6 new).
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- `npx expo config --type prebuild` resolves `runtimeVersion {policy: fingerprint}` and the updates block.
- `npx expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve --platform ios` computes a fingerprint locally.
- After merge: an EAS build 6 installs, then a test `eas update --channel preview` is received by the preview build.
**Promotion triggers:** enabling update code signing; changing the runtime policy after a store build has shipped; any `checkAutomatically` / `fallbackToCacheTimeout` change that blocks launch.

---

## Summary (plain language)

- **Installed `expo-updates`** with `npx expo install expo-updates` (→ `~56.0.28`, the SDK 56 match).
  - The lockfile gets only the 7 new package entries. I merged them into the existing lock so the npm-11 `libc` fields are kept (a local npm 10 would otherwise strip them).
  - The config plugin is applied automatically at prebuild: `expo-updates` is in `@expo/prebuild-config`'s versioned SDK plugins, so no `plugins` entry is needed.
- **app.json:**
  - `runtimeVersion: { "policy": "fingerprint" }`
  - `updates: { enabled: true, url: "https://u.expo.dev/a12c3345-cc8c-4c2c-9c57-711c10a57c1c", checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD", fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0 }`
  - `ios.buildNumber` "6"
  - `android.versionCode` 5
- **eas.json:** `production.channel = "production"`, `preview.channel = "preview"`. The development profile has no channel (it is a dev client).
- **Why fingerprint and not appVersion.** We keep `version` at `1.0.0` and bump only build numbers (`appVersionSource: local`). Under `appVersion`, every build would share runtime `1.0.0`. An update made after a native change (for example the HealthKit decision in C11) would then also reach older binaries that lack that native code, and could crash them. `fingerprint` hashes the native inputs, so any native change creates a new runtime and incompatible updates are never delivered. This is the Expo-recommended default for CNG projects like this one (no committed `ios/`/`android/`). Trade-off: publish from the same commit, or one with the same native inputs, as the target build. `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md` shows how to check.
- **Launch behaviour:** `ON_LOAD` checks on each cold start. `fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0` means launch never waits on the network; a downloaded update applies on the next launch.
- **Guard:** `scripts/validate-app-config.js` gained `validateUpdates`. When `expo-updates` is installed it fails if any of these is missing or wrong: `runtimeVersion`, an updates URL matching `extra.eas.projectId`, `fallbackToCacheTimeout` of 0, a valid `checkAutomatically`, and the per-profile channels.

## Owner action (no code secret required)
**The Expo project owner (`the-growth-project` account) must turn on EAS Update for project `a12c3345-…` once.** Do this on expo.dev → project → Updates, or by running `eas update:configure` as an account member. After that the operator publishes with `eas update --channel production|preview`. Builds ≤ #5 do not contain `expo-updates` and never receive updates; build 6 is the first that does. I did not run `eas build` / `eas submit`.

## Not touched
App JS code, importer / Roman P2 import paths.

## Test commands and results
```
npx jest --maxWorkers=1 scripts/__tests__                    # 2 suites, 32 passed (6 new in validateAppConfigUpdates.test.js)
npx jest --maxWorkers=1 App.test.tsx src/navigation/__tests__/linkingConfig.test.ts   # 11 passed
npx tsc --noEmit                                              # exit 0
npm run validate:config                                       # OK (2 pre-existing warnings)
npx expo config --type prebuild --json                        # runtimeVersion {policy: fingerprint}, updates block resolved
npx expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve --platform ios        # fingerprint computed (8fcef145…)
```
Lint: CI lints `src/**` only. `scripts/validate-app-config.js:42-43` has 2 pre-existing `no-var-requires` errors on lines this PR did not change.

Independent of #303 / #304. Merge order note: if #304 lands first, its `eas.json` env addition merges cleanly next to the new `channel` keys. Do not merge until audited.

---

## Audit fix round (AUDIT_mobile_305_e186e06e) → head `1b88f42`

**Now stacked on #304** (base `clinic/m2-core-polish`, reached by merging it in, no history rewrite). The purchase gate is a prerequisite of the OTA-enabled release, and the combined invariant is tested on one tree. Retarget to `main` after #304 merges.

| # | Finding | Fix | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | OTA could enable purchase surfaces | **Runtime:** fail-closed gate anchored to the native build (in #304). On iOS build ≥ 6, non-P2P purchases stay hidden whatever the bundle flag, and an unreadable build counts as hidden. **Server:** requests carry `X-Client-Platform` / `X-Client-Native-Build` / `X-Client-Purchase-Policy`; backend rejection of non-P2P sessions for iOS is listed as a follow-up. **Governance:** `npm run update:publish` (`scripts/eas-update-guard.js`) refuses to publish unless `--environment` equals the channel, `src/config/purchaseSurfaces.ts` matches `scripts/purchase-policy.sha256`, and the flag is `"true"` in the target EAS environment (via `eas env:exec`; fails closed). The docs say plainly that this is governance: a publisher with EAS rights can still ship arbitrary JS. | `iosNonP2PSurfacesMatrix.test.tsx` (the "OTA flips flag off" rows stay hidden with real surfaces; 1:1 and Android unchanged); `easUpdateGuard.test.js` (args, env value, lock matches, an edited gate is refused) |
| B1 | Publish commands omitted `--environment` | The runbook uses `npm run update:publish -- --channel production --environment production --message "…"` (and preview), and shows the raw equivalent with `--environment`. It documents build env vs update env, `eas env:create` for the hide flag in both environments, and the rest of the `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` set. | `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md` |
| C1 | Validator too permissive | Pins `{policy:"fingerprint"}` and rejects appVersion, sdkVersion, fixed strings and per-platform overrides. Rejects `disableAntiBrickingMeasures:true` and `useEmbeddedUpdate:false`. Requires the hide flag `"true"` in the preview and production profiles. | 9 new mutation tests (15/15) |
| C2 | Native crash/rollback untested | Runbook lists the required device checks before the first production publish (offline start, preview receipt, early-failure recovery, `eas update:rollback`). **Not performed.** | Docs |
| C3 | Unsigned updates | Posture documented and accepted: restrict EAS publish rights; signing is not the A1 fix. | Docs |

Local: scripts + config + matrix = 11 suites / 204 passed; validate:config OK; tsc clean.

---

## Re-audit fix round (AUDIT_mobile_305_1b88f424) → head `0897487`

| # | Finding | Fix | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | A JS-only threshold change keeps the same runtime | `fingerprint.config.js` adds `src/config/purchaseSurfaces.ts` to `extraSources`. Any gate edit now resolves to a new runtime and has to ship in a store build (owner-accepted trade-off). The validator fails if the entry is removed. | `expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve --platform ios`: head `4e762524…`, threshold 600 `89a39ee6…`. Without the config both are `a6122b73…` (reproduces the audit). `scripts/fingerprint-gate-check.js` + `purchaseGateFingerprint.test.js`: on iOS and Android, both threshold 600 and always-show change the runtime, and every non-gate source is byte-identical. |
| B2 | Local shell "true" confirmed as the remote value | The guard reads the remote value with `eas env:get <env> --variable-name FLAG --format short --scope project --non-interactive`, with the flag stripped from the child env. It requires exactly one `FLAG=true` record. It refuses a missing value ("not found" exits 0), empty, masked, duplicate, lookup or spawn failure, or a local non-true value. The publish child also runs without the local flag. | `easUpdateGuard.test.js` drives `main()` with an injected runner: remote missing / empty / false / masked / duplicate with local true, lookup failure, spawn failure, mismatch, local false, modified hash all refuse and never publish. Remote true publishes with `--environment`. Dry run never publishes. |
| B3 | Inherited community bypass | Fixed in #304 (`a3d40c4`, merged here) | Matrix |
| C1 | Validator ignores `environment` / deleted profiles | Requires the preview and production profiles, and `environment === channel` | 3 new mutation tests plus 3 fingerprint-config tests |
| C2 | Device/EAS evidence | Unchanged: the device checks are a hard pre-publish condition, not performed | Docs |
| C3 | Inherited docs and push lifecycle | Fixed in #304 | — |

Local: validator + guard 39/39; fingerprint 2/2; validate:config OK; tsc clean. Owner-accepted trade-off: gate-file edits require a new store build.

**Update:** merged #304 `3d9ab11` (which now includes main) at `157b723`. tsc clean; policy lock matches; validate:config OK.

**Update:** the first CI run at 157b723 failed 7 cases in `scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfig.test.js`. That test's tmp workspace did not copy the new `fingerprint.config.js` required by the validator. Fixed at `4578715`; scripts/__tests__ now passes 4 suites / 67 tests locally.
